::: {.lede}
I'm a Computer Science undergraduate at **Penn State**, College of Engineering,
graduating May 2028.
:::

Most of what I do sits between software engineering and statistics. I build systematic
trading strategies, but more of the hours go into the infrastructure. That is the part
that keeps a strategy running unattended without quietly turning into a different
strategy than the one I tested.

I founded **Weaver Capital LP** in January 2026 and run a multi-strategy systematic
portfolio there, across futures and equities on intraday, swing, and macro horizons.
Two of the strategies are live: [Rime](rime.html), a daily ETF regime allocator, and
[Fifth Sanctuary](fifth-sanctuary.html), an intraday gold volatility-expansion system.
I wrote the execution infrastructure too, in Python and C#, with automated strategy
synchronization, enforced position and drawdown limits, atomic state persistence across
restarts, and sub-second order handling. I also built the data pipelines and the
portfolio optimization that allocates capital across uncorrelated sleeves.

Since August 2026 I have also been an undergraduate researcher in the **Locomotion in
Biology and Robotics (LiBR) Lab** under Dr. Baxi Chong, building physics simulations of
multi-body contact dynamics in MuJoCo. I model an articulated three-section snake robot
navigating confined tunnel geometry, evaluating gait strategies in simulation before
hardware testing, and I am working on scaling laws for computational versus mechanical
cost of transport. It is a long way from futures, which is part of why I wanted it. The
common thread is controlling a system you can only partially observe.

In summer 2024 I was a research intern with the **Robot Perception and Navigation Group
at the University of Delaware**, where I built a 2D SLAM pipeline on a TurtleBot3 in C++
with ROS 2 and Google Cartographer, then integrated Nav2 for autonomous waypoint
navigation on the resulting map.

Before college I founded [FTC #16468 Green Lemons Robotics](robotics.html) and ran it
for six seasons, writing the autonomous control software in Java. We finished #1 OPR
globally among more than 8,000 teams at the 2024 World Championships.

## What I'm looking for

Summer 2027 internships in software engineering, quantitative development, or
quantitative research. I am most useful where the modeling and the systems work are the
same problem: research infrastructure, backtesting and simulation frameworks, execution
systems, and data pipelines that have to be correct.
